sheets.prompt:
Image 1 is a sticker of an octopus character. Draw this exact octopus character as a cut-out paper puppet: its separate body parts laid out on one sheet, the same drawing style, colours, texture, line and proportions as in image 1, every part at the size it has in image 1.

Draw each part on its own, spread out over the sheet with wide empty gaps between them, no part touching or overlapping another:
1. the body: the big round orange head with its darker spots and the short skirt below it where all the arms meet, facing the viewer as in image 1, without any arms, with a completely blank face — no eyes, no brows, no mouth — keep the two rosy cheeks; the skirt's bottom edge rounded.
2. an arm curled up high: one orange arm with its pale suckers, rising up and curling over at the tip, like the upper arm on the left of image 1, drawn whole, with a rounded base.
3. an arm out to the side: one orange arm with its pale suckers, reaching out sideways and curling down at the tip, like the arm on the far left of image 1, drawn whole, with a rounded base.
4. an arm reaching down: one orange arm with its pale suckers, reaching down and curling round at the tip, like the lower arms in image 1, drawn whole, with a rounded base.
5. the front arm: the arm in the middle at the bottom of image 1, curling round in a loop, drawn whole, with a rounded base.
6. the hugging arms: two orange arms with their pale suckers crossed over each other in front, wrapping round in a hug, drawn as one piece.

Every part is drawn whole, including what is normally hidden behind another part, and each joint end (where it tucks under the body or the head) is a full, smooth, rounded edge. No text, no labels, no numbers, no outline around the parts beyond the drawing's own line, no shadows. Fully transparent background.

Image 1 is a sticker of an octopus character; image 2 shows the same octopus cut into puppet parts, with a blank face. Draw the octopus's face pieces as separate stickers on one sheet: the same drawing style, colours and line as in image 1, every piece at the size it has on the octopus in image 1, so it fits the blank face in image 2.

Draw each piece on its own, spread out in tidy rows with wide empty gaps between them, nothing touching:
1. the octopus's eye as it is in image 1: a big dark brown round eye with a white sparkle.
2. the same eye wide open and surprised: bigger and rounder, with its white sparkle.
3. the same eye gently closed in sleep: a soft downward-curving line with a few lashes.
4. the same eye closed in a happy smile: an upward-curving arc.
5. the same eye sad: the pupil looking down, its upper lid drooping and tilted, a thin shine of a welling tear along the bottom rim.
6. the same eye crying: gently squeezed shut, a soft downward-curving line (a sad closed eye, not a smile), a few small lashes, and one small light-blue teardrop just below it.
7. the brow: the short brown curved brow line above an eye in image 1.
8. the mouth as it is in image 1: a small happy smile.
9. the mouth laughing: open wide, a little pink inside.
10. the mouth a small round "o".
11. the mouth sad: a small downturned frown.

No text, no labels, no numbers, no shadows, no face or head around the pieces. Fully transparent background.
